title: Find products that win on two measures
description: Compare revenue leaders with products bought by the most customers.
questions: Show our top 5 products by revenue and, separately, by distinct customers in Q2 2025.
Which products appear in both rankings?
For just those shared products, show revenue and distinct customers side by side.
expectation: The follow-ups should keep only products present in both displayed lists, without fetching a different population.

title: Explore customer value
description: Start with high spenders, then compare the value of their orders.
questions: Show our top 5 customers by revenue in 2025, using customer IDs.
Add their order counts and average order value.
Keep the three customers with the highest average order value among these five.
expectation: Average order value means revenue divided by distinct orders. The final selection comes from the five shown customers, not a new global ranking.

title: Find peak months and reorder the result
description: Find the strongest months while keeping the original figures intact.
questions: Show our monthly revenue, orders and distinct customers for 2025.
Keep the three months with the highest revenue, including their revenue and order counts.
Show those same three months in chronological order instead.
expectation: The last turn should change only the order of the selected months, preserving their values and columns.

title: Compare categories and ask how the answer was calculated
description: Use a natural-language follow-up, then ask the analyst to explain the arithmetic.
questions: Show our top 8 product categories by revenue in 2025. Include revenue, orders, distinct customers, and revenue per order.
Which of those categories had the highest revenue per order, and how many orders did it have?
How did you work that out? Explain the calculation in plain English.
expectation: The short answer and explanation are written by Gemini from verified facts. The explanation should use the selected category's revenue and orders, with no fresh database query.

title: Compare quarters fairly
description: Distinguish a change in total sales from a change in revenue per calendar day.
questions: Compare our total revenue in Q1 2026 with Q4 2025. Show the absolute and percentage change, using Q4 2025 as the baseline.
Add average daily revenue and the number of calendar days for both quarters.
Explain how you calculated the revenue percentage change and why the daily comparison can differ.
expectation: The baseline must remain Q4 2025. Daily revenue uses calendar days, including days with no sales; the explanation should not invent a cause for the change.

title: Investigate inactivity without assuming a spike
description: Check the premise, then change the inactivity definition explicitly.
questions: Did our customer inactivity rate increase during Q4 2025? Use a 90-day inactivity threshold and show eligible and inactive customer counts at both quarter boundaries.
Repeat the same analysis with a 60-day inactivity threshold.
Explain what this inactivity percentage means and which customers are included.
expectation: The agent should verify the direction from the data, preserve the quarter, and apply the new 60-day definition. An empty eligible cohort is undefined, not a zero-percent rate.

title: Draft a report, then save it explicitly
description: Prepare an analytical draft with next steps before adding it to your private library.
questions: Prepare a Q2 2025 sales report with total revenue, monthly revenue, top 5 products and recommended actions for Q3 2025. Do not save it yet.
Save it as "Q2 demo review".
List my saved reports.
expectation: The first turn must not save anything. Suggested actions are proposals, not proven causes or invented numeric targets. After the second turn, the report should appear in your own library.
